content.text: All preferred elements are present in § 20 and the indemnity is uncapped via the Excluded Claims definition — no redline needed.

input.quote: 20.1 Vendor shall defend, indemnify, and hold harmless Customer, its Affiliates, and their directors, officers, employees, and agents from each third-party claim and resulting damages, settlements, judgments, penalties, costs, and reasonable attorneys' fees arising from an allegation that the Services or Deliverables infringe or misappropriate an intellectual property right.
input.rationale: Section 20 meets our preferred position in full. Vendor expressly defends, indemnifies and holds harmless Customer and its Affiliates against third-party claims (20.1, 20.2), covering IP infringement/misappropriation by the Services or Deliverables (20.1) and Vendor's breach of Applicable Law, unauthorized access to or disclosure of Customer Data caused by Vendor, and Vendor's gross negligence, wilful misconduct or fraud (20.2). Section 20.4 supplies the standard procedure: prompt notice, reasonable cooperation at the indemnifying Party's expense, and control of the defence. Customer's reciprocal indemnity in 20.3 stays narrow — unmodified Customer-supplied material used strictly as authorized, and Customer's violation of Applicable Law — with carve-outs for Vendor Technology, modifications, combinations and instructions. Section 21 does not undercut this: "Excluded Claims" in 21.3 expressly includes a Party's indemnification obligations, so the Vendor indemnity sits outside the mutual liability cap (better than the fallback 3× super-cap). Section 20.5 also provides procure/modify/replace and refund remedies. No redline required.
